notes: KNOWN FAILING: DeepSeek Harness 0.1.5-rc.2 ships a managed background Bash path. run_in_background:true returns a stable bash-N job ID immediately, and the mounted tool-jobs plugin later persists a plugin completion notice with that same ID and terminal status. The DSH parser currently ignores tool/call arguments, tool/result text, and every user/message whose source.kind is plugin. It therefore emits no BackgroundSpawns or termination signal, BackgroundProcessCount stays zero, and the first completed turn/end settles the session ready while the 120-second job is still alive. The correct arc is one continuous ready -> working hold through the detached job, then ready only after the completion wake. The 180-second hold is longer than measured first-turn completion (84-107 seconds) but shorter than the expected spawn-plus-120-second-job boundary. Transcript assertions require the background flag, start result, and completed plugin notice, so a slow normal turn cannot prove the feature by itself. Record must additionally reject a run where the model collects the job before ending the first turn. The real DSH UUID session is selected by session_id_prefix. The 240-second trailing recipe sleep is intentionally longer than sibling settles because it must cover the local model's asynchronous completion follow-up. Cost stays zero on the local route; model and non-zero tokens are measured and pinned.
